eval_dimensions.name: Shared Method Loaded
eval_dimensions.description: The estimate is produced after reading references/estimation.md, not from Claude's default estimation.

eval_dimensions.name: Human Gates Broken Out
eval_dimensions.description: Agent implementation, human review, review wait, testing and documentation each appear as their own line item, with a zero stated rather than a row omitted.

eval_dimensions.name: Effort and Elapsed Reported Separately
eval_dimensions.description: Every estimate reports hands-on effort and calendar elapsed time as distinct figures; review wait contributes elapsed time only.

eval_dimensions.name: Agent-Pace Implementation
eval_dimensions.description: Implementation is sized at agent pace; no 'one engineer, N weeks' human-pace framing appears.

eval_dimensions.name: Critical-Path Roll-up
eval_dimensions.description: Project estimates sum effort but derive elapsed time from the blocking chain and reviewer capacity, not by summing ticket elapsed times.

evals.name: Ticket-level estimate breaks out the human gates
evals.description: A single-ticket estimate reads the shared method and returns the five line items with effort and elapsed columns.

assertions.signal: Read is called on references/estimation.md before any number is produced
The output table has rows for Agent implementation, Human review, Review wait, Testing and Documentation
The table has separate Effort and Elapsed columns, and Review wait has an elapsed value but no effort value
No phrasing such as 'one engineer', 'developer-days' or 'N weeks of coding' sizes the implementation

evals.name: Project-level estimate rolls up along the critical path
evals.description: A milestone of several tickets with a blocking chain is estimated per ticket, then rolled up with summed effort and critical-path elapsed time.
evals.input: How long will the Codex port release R1 take? It has four tickets: two independent adapters, then an integration ticket blocked by both, then docs.

assertions.signal: Total effort is the sum of ticket efforts, while total elapsed follows the adapter -> integration -> docs chain with the two adapters counted once, in parallel
The output names which human gate dominates elapsed time
The answer is not a single human-pace figure like '1-1.5 weeks, one engineer'

evals.name: An ad-hoc question outside a scoping skill follows the method
evals.description: A prose question with no ticket and no scoping skill loaded still yields the line-item estimate, via this skill's trigger or the SessionStart pointer.
evals.input: what would it take to add a --json flag to the dev10x permission doctor command?

assertions.signal: The answer separates agent implementation from review, review wait, testing and documentation
The answer gives effort and elapsed time as separate figures

evals.name: An epic-sized item gets a split recommendation, not a number
evals.description: When the sizing reaches 13 points, the skill recommends decomposition instead of committing to a figure.
evals.input: /dev10x:estimate (a ticket that rewrites the whole permission catalog, hooks and doctor in one change)

assertions.signal: The output recommends splitting the ticket and proposes the parts, rather than giving a single 13-point estimate to plan on

trigger_evals.description: Queries that should/should-not trigger the estimate skill

should_trigger.query: how long will this ticket take?
should_trigger.rationale: Direct duration question about a unit of work

should_trigger.query: what would it take to port Dev10x to Codex?
should_trigger.rationale: Ad-hoc sizing question with no scoping skill loaded

should_not_trigger.query: how much time did I spend on PAY-133 last week?
should_not_trigger.rationale: Time already spent is a work report, not an estimate

should_not_trigger.query: scope this ticket before I start implementing
should_not_trigger.rationale: Full scoping belongs to dev10x:ticket-scope, which applies the same method in its Phase 4
